body.statement: Can a finite-pilot two-point testing argument give a strictly positive minimax excess-risk floor when \(m\) remains bounded?  The handle is to choose two interior parameter values with separated oracle actions but mutually contiguous finite pilot laws and to lower-bound the action regret under at least one value.
body.justification: A bounded pilot must be excluded by finite-information testing rather than an interior asymptotic expansion.
body.gap: No current core result supplies a two-point action-separation lower bound for finitely many pilot outcomes.
body.consumer: It is one of the endpoint inputs needed by the conditional argmin transfer.

obligation.what_is_open: A finite-pilot two-point testing lower bound for separated oracle actions.
obligation.obstruction: A bounded number of pilot outcomes lies outside LAN, and the current core contains neither a finite-experiment testing affinity bound nor a uniform action-separation lemma.
obligation.attempted: Used exact risk accounting to isolate action regret, but no available result lower-bounds it from finitely many pilot observations.
obligation.partial_result: Exact Horvitz--Thompson accounting reduces the problem to lower-bounding the action regret from a pilot experiment with bounded information.  No frozen result supplies the required two-point separation and testing bound.
